result.summary: 这篇论文提出了“精度感知”的缩放定律，用以预测语言模型在低精度训练和训练后量化下的损失变化 [abstract]。作者将低精度训练建模为降低模型的有效参数量，并在超过 465 次预训练运行上拟合，验证了最高 1.7B 参数、26B token 的模型 [abstract]。研究发现，训练后量化带来的退化随训练数据量增加而增大，最终可能使额外的预训练数据变得有害 [abstract]；而在训练方面，缩放定律表明在更低精度下训练更大的模型可能是计算最优的 [abstract]。作者将训练后量化与预训练量化的缩放定律统一为单一函数形式，用以预测不同精度下训练和推理的退化 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 论文要回答的问题是：精度、参数量与数据量之间存在怎样的权衡，以及这些权衡在预训练和推理时有何不同 [S1.p1]。作者指出，精度是同时影响成本和性能的第三个重要因素，而当前的缩放定律并未将其纳入考量 [S1.p1][abstract]。

evidence.quote: However, the precision in which models are trained and served is an important third factor that contributes to both cost and performance.
Specifically, we ask: What are the tradeoffs between precision, parameters, and data? How do they compare for pretraining and inference?
Low precision training and inference affect both the quality and cost of language models, but current scaling laws do not account for this.

method.text: 作者提出“精度感知”的缩放定律，其核心思想是假设比特精度与参数量可互换地共同决定模型的“有效参数量” N_eff，而量化实现细节仅通过影响该量来作用于损失缩放 [S1.p2]。对于训练，作者将低精度训练建模为降低有效参数量，并给出统一形式 L(N,D,P_train,P_post)=AN_eff^{-α}+BD^{-β}+E+δ_PTQ [S1.p4]。对于训练后量化，作者用 GPTQ 量化 BF16 训练的模型，量化退化 δ_PTQ 被建模为包含“过训练效应”和“鲁棒化效应”的函数 [S3.p1][S5.p4]。

evidence.quote: This functional form that posits bit precision and parameter count interchangeably contribute to a model’s “effective parameter count,” $N_{\text{eff}}$
implementation details like which parts of a model are quantized to what precision, interact with loss scaling only through their effect on this quantity.

we ultimately find a unified scaling law that takes the following form: $L(N,D,P_{\text{train}},P_{\text{post}})=\underbrace{\underbrace{AN_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha}}_{\text{Training-time Effects}}+BD^{-\beta}+E}_{\text{Usual Chinchilla form}}+\underbrace{\delta_{\text{PTQ}}(N_{\text{eff}},D,P_{\text{train}},P_{\text{post}})}_{\text{Post-Training Effects}}$
we consider models trained in BF16 and use GPTQ to post-train quantize them

$\delta_{\text{PTQ}}(N,D,P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{post}})=C_{T}e^{-P_{\text{post}}/\gamma_{\text{post}}}\underbrace{\left(\frac{D^{\gamma_{D}}}{N_{\text{eff}}^{\gamma_{N}}}\right)}_{\text{Overtraining effect}}\underbrace{[1-e^{-C_{\text{w}}(P_{\text{w}}-P_{\text{post}})}]}_{\text{Robustification effect}}$

experiments.text: 作者在 Dolma V1.7 数据集上训练并评估了一系列 OLMo 风格的模型，使用标准 Transformer++ 实现 [S2.SS3.p1]。实验扫描了 N∈[30,60,110,220] 百万非嵌入参数和 D∈[1.5,3,6,13,26] 十亿 token，每个 (N,D) 组合运行超过 20 次，并扫描 8 种精度值 [S2.SS3.p1]。训练精度扫描覆盖权重、激活和 KV 缓存的 P_w,P_a,P_kv∈[3,12]，并包含 BF16 基线 [S4.p1]。作者还在更大规模上验证预测，训练了从 FP4 到 FP32、220M 到 1.6B 参数的计算匹配模型 [S4.SS3.SSS2.p2]。

evidence.quote: We train and evaluate a suite of OLMo-style models on the Dolma V1.7 dataset, using a standard Transformer++ implementation
Our experiments consist of a sweep of language model pretraining runs over $N\in[30,60,110,220]$ million parameters (non-embedding) and $D\in[1.5,3,6,13,26]$ billion tokens.
we sweep 8 values of precision for each of the (weights, activations, attention).
We sweep the training precisions of the weights, activations, and KV cache $P_{\text{w}},P_{\text{a}},P_{\text{kv}}\in[3,12]$ individually, as well as training BF16 baselines.
We train compute-matched models at various parameter count and precision ranging from FP4 to FP32 and 220M to 1.6B parameters.

findings.text: 训练后量化引起的退化随数据量增加而增大，因此对于固定模型，在某个点之后继续用更多数据训练，如果模型之后会被量化，可能反而有害 [S1.p3]。在训练方面，缩放定律表明计算最优的预训练精度通常与计算预算无关 [S1.p3]；但如果模型大小 N 被固定，这一独立性不再成立，此时计算最优精度随计算量缓慢增长，约为 P*∝log C [S1.p3][S4.SS3.SSS3.p1]。作者还发现，权重比特精度可以与参数量互换，且精度提升的收益在低精度时较大、在高精度（约 6-7 比特）时饱和 [S4.SS1.p1]。统一缩放定律在超过 1000 个数据点上取得 R²=0.90 的拟合 [S5.p6]。

evidence.quote: We find that the degradation increases with data, so that for a fixed model, training on additional data after a certain point can be actively harmful if the model will be quantized after training.
Our scaling laws for pretraining suggest that the compute-optimal pretraining precision is in general independent of compute budget.
this independence ceases to be true if model size is constrained, in which case the compute-optimal precision grows slowly in compute.
our scaling laws predict that models of differing sizes should not necessarily be trained in the same precision, and that compute-optimal precision scales as $P^{*}(C)\propto\log C$.
the bit precision of the weights can be traded off for the number of parameters
the gains from increasing the bit precision of the weights are large at lower precisions but saturate at higher precisions (typically around 6-7 bits per weight).
we find a strong fit with $R^{2}=0.90$ on over 1000 data points

limitations.text: 作者指出，分析中始终使用固定架构来受控地考察精度、参数和 token 的影响，而低精度训练常涉及架构调整，可以缩小与普通全精度模型的差距 [S6.p2]。其次，虽然计算成本随精度线性缩放，但由于系统开销，将精度减半带来的收益通常不到 2 倍 [S6.p2]。第三，作者只考虑损失缩放，没有进行下游模型评估 [S6.p2]。作者强调所发现的趋势旨在提供启示而非规定性结论，并希望未来工作在更大模型规模上更全面地检验这些效应 [S6.p2]。

evidence.quote: First, we use a fixed architecture throughout to examine the effects of precision, parameters, and tokens in a controlled manner.
In contrast, low precision training often involves architectural tweaks that can close much of the gap from a vanilla full precision model.
Second, while compute costs do scale linearly with precision, the gains from halving precision are usually less than 2x due to systems overhead.
Third, we only consider loss scaling without downstream model evaluations.
We emphasize that the trends we find aim to be suggestive rather than prescriptive, and hope future work can more comprehensively examine these effects at larger model scale.

issues.quote: we find a strong fit with $R^{2}=0.90$ on over 1000 data points
